regional.syndrome: Short febrile illness with headache and myalgia.
regional.headline: Group C viruses repeatedly isolated from febrile Amazonian patients.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Dengue fever: high fever, severe headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia/arthralgia ('breakbone fever'), rash. A minority progress at defervescence to dengue with warning signs or severe dengue — plasma leakage, shock, haemorrhage and organ impairment. Secondary infection with a different serotype raises severe-disease risk through antibody-dependent enhancement.
regional.headline: The most important arboviral infection of humans worldwide, with an estimated 100–400 million infections annually.
regional.prevention: Vector control, Wolbachia-based mosquito replacement, and the live-attenuated vaccines CYD-TDV (serostatus-restricted) and TAK-003.
regional.geography: Tropics and subtropics worldwide; expanding with vector range.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Biphasic: an initial fever with headache and myalgia, brief remission, then in ~15% a toxic phase with jaundice, haemorrhage, renal failure and shock; case fatality in the toxic phase is 30–60%.
regional.headline: The prototype flavivirus and the reason the genus is named 'flavi' — a vaccine-preventable viral haemorrhagic fever.
regional.prevention: A single dose of the 17D live-attenuated vaccine gives lifelong protection — one of the most effective vaccines ever made; mandated under International Health Regulations for travel to endemic areas.
regional.geography: Tropical South America and sub-Saharan Africa.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Usually mild or asymptomatic: low-grade fever, maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis, arthralgia. Congenital Zika syndrome — microcephaly, cerebral calcification, ocular and joint anomalies — follows infection in pregnancy. Guillain–Barré syndrome is an established post-infectious complication.
regional.headline: Flavivirus whose 2015–2016 American epidemic established it as a human teratogen.
regional.prevention: Vector control, barrier contraception or abstinence after exposure, travel advice in pregnancy. No licensed vaccine.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.headline: Mucambo virus. VEE complex; sporadic human febrile illness.
regional.geography: Mucambo virus. VEE complex; sporadic human febrile illness.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.common: Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV), subtypes IAB/IC/ID/IE
regional.syndrome: Influenza-like illness with fever, headache, myalgia and prostration in most; encephalitis in ~4% of children and <1% of adults. Infection in pregnancy can cause fetal loss.
regional.headline: Epizootic alphavirus causing large human and equine outbreaks in the Americas; also a classical laboratory-acquired infection.
regional.prevention: Equine vaccination (which interrupts amplification), vector control, and biosafety containment in laboratories.
regional.geography: Central and South America, with historical incursions into Texas.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.headline: Mayaro virus. Febrile arthralgic illness in South America.
regional.geography: Mayaro virus. Febrile arthralgic illness in South America.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.headline: Hepatitis D virus genotype 8. West Africa and, through migration, South America.
regional.geography: Hepatitis D virus genotype 8. West Africa and, through migration, South America.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: No defined human syndrome; serological cross-reactivity within the clade complicates attribution.

regional.geography: Trinidad, South America, Southeast Asia (clade members).
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.
